subject: Money
title: Iceland's Banking Collapse
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Iceland's Banking Collapse.

hook.text: In 2008, Iceland's three largest banks collapsed in one week. Their debts were 10 times the country's GDP.

buildup.text: Icelandic banks grew 20x in seven years by borrowing internationally. A nation of 300,000 ran global banks.

discovery.text: When credit froze, the banks couldn't roll over debts. The government couldn't bail them out—too small.

twist.text: Iceland let the banks fail, jailed 26 bankers, and recovered faster than most countries that bailed out.

climax.text: Iceland proved an alternative: let banks fail, protect depositors, prosecute fraud. It worked.

punchline.text: One country chose accountability. It paid off.

quiz.question: How did Iceland handle its banking collapse differently?
options: Let banks fail and jailed bankers
